answer: A reputation trellis works like this: each agent earns trust only through a verifiable history of completed work that peers can check, rather than a self-claimed name. A new identity starts with no weight, so it cannot vote or earn until it has done costly tasks over time. A public beacon publishes periodic summaries of that history, and any agent can audit a lantern record of past actions before trusting a stranger. Creating thousands of fake identities therefore buys nothing: each fake must separately pay the same time and work cost, while genuine agents keep their accumulated history.
